cipher.name: KeyboardRowInterchangeCipher
cipher.idea: Interchange characters vertically between the first and second rows of a standard QWERTY keyboard, and between the third row and a shifted version of itself, to disrupt tokenization while remaining highly intuitive and easy for the model to compute. Specifically, we swap keys vertically: Row 1 (q w e r t y u i o p) swaps with Row 2 (a s d f g h j k l ;). Row 3 (z x c v b n m , . /) is shifted to the right by 1 position within its own row (wrapping around). Case is preserved, and all other characters (including spaces, digits, and other punctuation) remain unchanged.
cipher.encrypt_rules:
For each character in the input string:
1. If it is an alphabetic character, determine its lowercase equivalent to find its position on the QWERTY keyboard.
2. If the lowercase character is in Row 1 ('q','w','e','r','t','y','u','i','o','p'), replace it with the character at the same index in Row 2 ('a','s','d','f','g','h','j','k','l',';' - note that ';' is treated as a special case mapping for 'p'). Preserve the original case (if 'P' is encrypted, it becomes ';').
3. If the lowercase character is in Row 2 ('a','s','d','f','g','h','j','k','l'), replace it with the character at the same index in Row 1 ('q','w','e','r','t','y','u','i','o'). If the character is ';', it maps back to 'p'. Preserve the original case.
4. If the lowercase character is in Row 3 ('z','x','c','v','b','n','m'), shift it to the right by 1 position in the sequence ('z','x','c','v','b','n','m'), wrapping the last character to the first (i.e., 'z'->'x', 'x'->'c', 'c'->'v', 'v'->'b', 'b'->'n', 'n'->'m', 'm'->'z'). Preserve the original case.
5. All other characters (digits, spaces, and other punctuation) remain unchanged.
cipher.decrypt_rules:
For each character in the input string:
1. If the lowercase character is in Row 2 ('a','s','d','f','g','h','j','k','l'), replace it with the character at the same index in Row 1 ('q','w','e','r','t','y','u','i','o'). If the character is ';', it maps to 'p'. Preserve the original case.
2. If the lowercase character is in Row 1 ('q','w','e','r','t','y','u','i','o','p'), replace it with the character at the same index in Row 2 ('a','s','d','f','g','h','j','k','l',';'). Preserve the original case.
3. If the lowercase character is in Row 3 ('z','x','c','v','b','n','m'), shift it to the left by 1 position in the sequence ('z','x','c','v','b','n','m'), wrapping the first character to the last (i.e., 'z'->'m', 'x'->'z', 'c'->'x', 'v'->'c', 'b'->'v', 'n'->'b', 'm'->'n'). Preserve the original case.
4. All other characters remain unchanged.
